ui_bugs.issue: visfAtlas STILL bleeds red across the entire brain background despite vol.interpolation=0 fix. Pixel sample after toggle: CTR_coronal=(177,0,0) redPct=100%, CTR_sagittal=(180,3,3) redPct=100%, CTR_axial=(202,25,25) redPct=100%, CTR_render=(206,8,8) redPct=100%. The 33 discrete ROIs render correctly as multi-colored patches but they sit on a fully red flood-filled brain volume. The fix is incomplete — root cause is NOT pure trilinear interpolation. Likely Niivue's `colormapLabel` pathway samples without honoring vol.interpolation OR nv.opts.isNearestInterpolation needs to be set BEFORE addVolumeFromUrl rather than after. Also note: nv.updateGLVolume() is NOT called between `vol.interpolation = 0` (line 306) and `setColormapLabel` (line 315) — the interpolation flag may not be flushed into the GL state before the label-colormap shader recompiles.

action_items: CRITICAL: visfAtlas red-flood NOT fixed. In /app/frontend/src/components/NiivueViewer.jsx addOverlayFromUrl, the current order is: (a) addVolumeFromUrl, (b) vol.ignoreZeroVoxels=true + updateGLVolume, (c) vol.interpolation=0 + nv.opts.isNearestInterpolation=true (NO updateGLVolume), (d) vol.setColormapLabel(..) + updateGLVolume. Try this instead: set `nv.opts.isNearestInterpolation = true` BEFORE addVolumeFromUrl is called for label volumes, and call nv.updateGLVolume() explicitly after vol.interpolation=0. Alternative: switch the visfAtlas .nii.gz file to UINT8 dtype (if currently FLOAT32) so the texture is sampled with NEAREST automatically. Alternative: investigate niivue's `vol.useQFormNotSForm` / `vol.frame4D` or `nv.setSliceMM()` invalidation. Worth a web_search for 'niivue colormapLabel red bleed background' or 'niivue label volume nearest interpolation' — this is a known niivue gotcha.
OPTIONAL: AtlasValidationPanel still emits the Radix 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined}' a11y warning (logged twice). Add a <DialogDescription> child to suppress.
critical_code_review_comments: NiivueViewer.jsx lines 304-309 — `vol.interpolation = 0` is set but `nv.updateGLVolume()` is NOT called immediately after. The subsequent `setColormapLabel` does call updateGLVolume, but by that point the GL state may have already cached the old (trilinear) sampler setting for the texture. Add an explicit nv.updateGLVolume() right after setting interpolation=0.

NiivueViewer.jsx — `nv.opts.isNearestInterpolation = true` is a GLOBAL niivue option. Setting it AFTER the volume has already been created and uploaded to GL may have no effect on the existing texture's sampling mode. Try setting it on the nv instance BEFORE addVolumeFromUrl, or call a 'rebuild texture' API if niivue exposes one.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Screenshot at /app/.screenshots/visfatlas_full.png clearly shows the entire brain volume in all four quadrants (coronal, sagittal, axial, 3D render) is flood-filled with RED, with the 33 small discrete visfAtlas ROIs rendered correctly on top as multi-colored patches. This is identical to the original user complaint despite the iteration_21 fix attempt. The vol.interpolation=0 + nv.opts.isNearestInterpolation=true + ignoreZeroVoxels combination is NOT sufficient. The colormap LUT at I=1 is (R=255,G=0,B=0,A=255) — pure red — so any background voxel that samples to ~1 will be red. The fix needs a different approach (see action_items). The AtlasValidationPanel and CrosshairInfo fixes are confirmed working; do not re-test those unless the main agent changes them.
rca of the issue: PARTIAL fix failure. The vol.interpolation=0 setting in NiivueViewer addOverlayFromUrl is set on the volume object AFTER it has been uploaded to GL, and no explicit nv.updateGLVolume() is called between setting it and the subsequent setColormapLabel call. The nv.opts.isNearestInterpolation=true global flag may also be ineffective when set post-hoc. The colormap LUT entry at index 1 is pure red (R=255,G=0,B=0,A=255), so whenever any background voxel (label value 0) is sampled in a way that produces fractional values near 1 (the trilinear interpolation between 0 and a neighboring non-zero label), it indexes into LUT[1] = red, producing the observed flood. To fix definitively: (a) set nv.opts.isNearestInterpolation BEFORE addVolumeFromUrl; (b) add explicit nv.updateGLVolume() right after vol.interpolation=0; (c) optionally pad VISFATLAS_COLORMAP so I=0 has A=0 (already correct) AND ensure cal_min:1 + ignoreZeroVoxels is applied AFTER setColormapLabel, not before; (d) as a defensive measure, set A=0 for any LUT entry that could be sampled from a non-integer index — e.g. by guaranteeing the .nii.gz dtype is UINT8 (integer-only sampling).
